questions.stem: What percentage of 300 is 75?
A fish swam a distance of 5,104 yards. How far did the fish swim, in miles? \((1 mile = 1,760 yards)\)

On the first day of a semester, a film club has 90 members. Each day after the first day of the semester, 10 new members join the film club. If no members leave the film club, how many total members will the film club have 4 days after the first day of the semester?
questions.explanation: Starting with 90 members and adding 10 per day for 4 days: \(90 + 10(4) = 90 + 40 = 130\).

questions.stem: The result of increasing the quantity \(x\) by 400% is 60. What is the value of \(x\)?
What is 20% of 440?
In 2008, Zinah earned 14% more than in 2007, and in 2009 Zinah earned 4% more than in 2008. If Zinah earned \(y\) times as much in 2009 as in 2007, what is the value of \(y\)?
questions.explanation: Earnings multiply by 1.14 then by 1.04: \(1.14 \times 1.04 = 1.1856\). So \(y = 1.1856\).

questions.stem: The ratio of the length of line segment \(XY\) to the length of line segment \(ZV\) is 6 to 1. If the length of line segment \(XY\) is 102 inches, what is the length, in inches, of line segment \(ZV\)?
Rectangle P has an area of 72 square inches. If a rectangle with an area of 20 square inches is removed from rectangle P, what is the area, in square inches, of the resulting figure?
questions.explanation: Removing 20 square inches from 72 square inches leaves \(72 - 20 = 52\) square inches.

questions.stem: A total of 165 people contributed to a charity event as either a donor or a volunteer. 130 people contributed as a donor. How many people contributed as a volunteer?
There are 250 trees in a park. Of these trees, 6% are birch trees. How many birch trees are in the park?
The number of raccoons in a 131-square-mile area is estimated to be 2,358. What is the estimated population density, in raccoons per square mile, of this area?
questions.explanation: Population density is \(\frac{2{,}358}{131} = 18\) raccoons per square mile.

questions.stem: The speed of a vehicle is increasing at a rate of 7.3 meters per second squared. What is this rate, in miles per minute squared, rounded to the nearest tenth? \((Use 1 mile = 1,609 meters.)\)
questions.explanation: Convert: \(7.3 \frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}^2} \times \frac{1 \text{ mile}}{1609 \text{ m}} \times \left(\frac{60 \text{ s}}{1 \text{ min}}\right)^2 = 7.3 \times \frac{3600}{1609} \approx 16.3\) miles per minute squared.

questions.stem: For a certain region, a table shows the average number of store employees in 2016 by type of store: warehouse store 365, department store 213, supermarket 130. Based on the table, how much greater was the average number of store employees in warehouse stores than in supermarkets?

A bowl contains 20 ounces of water. When the bowl is uncovered, the amount of water in the bowl decreases by 1 ounce every 4 days. If 9 ounces of water remain in this bowl, for how many days has it been uncovered?
questions.explanation: The water decreased by \(20 - 9 = 11\) ounces. At 1 ounce per 4 days, that is \(11 \times 4 = 44\) days.

questions.stem: Ty set a goal to walk at least 24 kilometers every day to prepare for a multiday hike. On a certain day, Ty plans to walk at an average speed of 4 kilometers per hour. What is the minimum number of hours Ty must walk on that day to fulfill the daily goal?
questions.explanation: Time equals distance divided by speed: \(\frac{24}{4} = 6\) hours.

questions.stem: One gallon of stain will cover 170 square feet of a surface. A yard has a total fence area of \(w\) square feet. Which equation represents the total amount of stain \(S\), in gallons, needed to stain the fence in this yard twice?
questions.explanation: Staining twice covers \(2w\) square feet. At 170 square feet per gallon, \(S = \frac{2w}{170} = \frac{w}{85}\).

questions.stem: A certain town has an area of 4.36 square miles. What is the area, in square yards, of this town? \((1 mile = 1,760 yards)\)
The result of increasing the quantity \(x\) by 1,800% is 684. What is the value of \(x\)?
questions.explanation: Increasing \(x\) by 1,800% multiplies it by \(1 + 18 = 19\), so \(19x = 684\), giving \(x = 36\).

questions.stem: An object's speed is 64 yards per second. What is the object's speed, in feet per second? \((1 yard = 3 feet)\)
questions.explanation: Multiply by 3 feet per yard: \(64 \times 3 = 192\) feet per second.

questions.stem: Of 300,000 paper clips, 234,000 are size large. What percentage of the paper clips are size large?
A shirt that costs \(40\) dollars is marked down by \(20\%\). What is the discount, in dollars?
\(12\) is what percent of \(48\)?
Write \(\tfrac{3}{5}\) as a percent.
A car travels \(150\) miles in \(3\) hours. What is its average speed, in miles per hour?
questions.explanation: Average speed is distance divided by time: \(150 \div 3 = 50\) miles per hour.

questions.stem: A recipe uses flour and sugar in the ratio \(3:1\). If \(6\) cups of flour are used, how many cups of sugar are needed?
questions.explanation: The ratio \(3:1\) means sugar is one third of the flour: \(6 \div 3 = 2\) cups.

questions.stem: What number is \(30\%\) of \(200\)?
A price of \(50\) dollars increases by \(10\%\). What is the new price, in dollars?
questions.explanation: The increase is \(0.10 \times 50 = 5\) dollars, so the new price is \(50 + 5 = 55\) dollars.

questions.stem: \(40\%\) of a number is \(20\). What is the number?
Convert \(0.045\) to a percent.
A store adds \(8\%\) sales tax to a \(25\) dollar purchase. What is the tax, in dollars?
The ratio of boys to girls in a class is \(2:3\). If there are \(10\) boys, how many girls are there?
questions.explanation: Each ratio unit is \(10 \div 2 = 5\) students, so girls \(= 3 \times 5 = 15\).

questions.stem: What is the average of \(12\), \(18\), and \(24\)?
A \(20\) dollar tip is what percent of a \(80\) dollar bill?
If \(3\) notebooks cost \(6\) dollars, what is the cost of \(5\) notebooks, in dollars?
questions.explanation: Each notebook costs \(6 \div 3 = 2\) dollars, so \(5\) cost \(5 \times 2 = 10\) dollars.

questions.stem: A number increased from \(20\) to \(25\). What is the percent increase?
questions.explanation: The increase is \(5\); as a percent of the original \(20\), \(\tfrac{5}{20} = 25\%\).

questions.stem: Solve the proportion \(\dfrac{x}{12} = \dfrac{3}{4}\).
After a \(20\%\) discount, a jacket costs \(48\) dollars. What was the original price, in dollars?
questions.explanation: The sale price is \(80\%\) of the original: \(0.80 x = 48\), so \(x = 48 \div 0.80 = 60\) dollars.

questions.stem: A price is increased by \(25\%\) and then decreased by \(20\%\). The final price is what percent of the original?
questions.explanation: Multiply the factors: \(1.25 \times 0.80 = 1.00\), so the price returns to \(100\%\).

questions.stem: On a test, a student answered \(42\) of \(50\) questions correctly. What percent were incorrect?
A solution is \(30\%\) acid. How many liters of acid are in \(40\) liters of solution?
The population of a town grew from \(2{,}500\) to \(2{,}900\). What is the percent increase?
A car uses \(4\) gallons of gas to travel \(96\) miles. At this rate, how many gallons are needed for \(240\) miles?
questions.explanation: The rate is \(96 \div 4 = 24\) miles per gallon, so \(240 \div 24 = 10\) gallons.

questions.stem: A class has \(12\) boys and \(18\) girls. What percent of the class is boys?
An item costing \(200\) dollars is marked up \(15\%\), then a \(10\) dollar coupon is applied. What is the final price, in dollars?
questions.explanation: After markup: \(200 \times 1.15 = 230\); minus the coupon: \(230 - 10 = 220\) dollars.

questions.stem: The ratio of red to blue marbles is \(5:3\). If there are \(64\) marbles in all, how many are blue?
questions.explanation: There are \(5 + 3 = 8\) parts, so each part is \(64 \div 8 = 8\) marbles; blue \(= 3 \times 8 = 24\).

questions.stem: A worker's hourly wage rises from \(16\) to \(20\) dollars. What is the percent increase?
A \(300\) dollar deposit earns \(6\%\) simple interest per year. How much interest is earned after \(2\) years, in dollars?
questions.explanation: Simple interest is \(P r t = 300 \times 0.06 \times 2 = 36\) dollars.

questions.stem: Two numbers are in the ratio \(4:7\), and the larger is \(63\). What is the smaller number?
questions.explanation: Each unit is \(63 \div 7 = 9\), so the smaller is \(4 \times 9 = 36\).

questions.stem: A shirt normally \(50\) dollars is on sale for \(35\) dollars. What is the percent discount?
A recipe for \(4\) servings needs \(3\) cups of rice. How many cups are needed for \(10\) servings?
questions.explanation: The rate is \(\tfrac34\) cup per serving, so \(10 \times \tfrac34 = 7.5\) cups.

questions.stem: A bag holds \(60\) candies: \(45\%\) are red. How many are not red?
A number is \(150\%\) of \(48\). What is the number?
A store buys an item for \(80\) dollars and sells it for \(100\) dollars. What is the percent profit based on cost?
questions.explanation: Profit is \(20\); as a percent of the \(80\) cost, \(\tfrac{20}{80} = 25\%\).

questions.stem: A measurement was recorded as \(52\) but the true value is \(50\). What is the percent error?
A cyclist rides \(30\) miles at \(15\) miles per hour, then \(30\) miles at \(10\) miles per hour. What is the average speed for the whole trip, in miles per hour?
questions.explanation: Total time is \(\tfrac{30}{15} + \tfrac{30}{10} = 2 + 3 = 5\) hours for \(60\) miles: \(60 \div 5 = 12\) miles per hour.

questions.stem: In a survey, \(35\%\) of \(240\) people chose option A. How many people chose option A?
A quantity increases by \(40\%\) to become \(70\). What was the original quantity?
A map uses a scale of \(1\) inch to \(25\) miles. Two cities are \(3.5\) inches apart on the map. How many miles apart are they?
A phone's price dropped \(10\%\) in March and another \(10\%\) in April. What is the total percent decrease from the original?
questions.explanation: The remaining fraction is \(0.90 \times 0.90 = 0.81\), a \(19\%\) total decrease.

questions.stem: A team won \(60\%\) of its first \(20\) games and \(75\%\) of its next \(20\) games. Over all \(40\) games, what percent did it win?
A price is increased by \(20\%\), then the new price is decreased by \(15\%\). What is the net percent change from the original?
questions.explanation: The combined factor is \(1.20 \times 0.85 = 1.02\), a net increase of \(2\%\).

questions.stem: A \(50\)-liter mixture is \(40\%\) acid. How many liters of pure acid must be added to make the mixture \(50\%\) acid?
A store's revenue rose \(25\%\) while the number of items sold fell \(20\%\). By what percent did the average price per item change?
questions.explanation: Price factor is \(\tfrac{1.25}{0.80} = 1.5625\), an increase of \(56.25\%\).

questions.stem: A blend mixes coffee A (costing \(8\) dollars per pound) and coffee B (\(12\) dollars per pound) to sell at \(9\) dollars per pound. What is the ratio of A to B, by weight?
questions.explanation: Using alligation, the distances from \(9\) are \(12 - 9 = 3\) (for A) and \(9 - 8 = 1\) (for B), so A:B \(= 3:1\).

questions.stem: The ratio of men to women at an event was \(3:2\). After \(20\) more women arrived, the ratio became \(3:4\). How many men were present?
An alloy is \(60\%\) copper. How many kilograms of pure copper must be added to \(40\) kg of the alloy to raise the copper content to \(75\%\)?
After a \(30\%\) discount and an additional \(10\%\) off the discounted price, a coat costs \(63\) dollars. What was the original price, in dollars?
questions.explanation: The price factor is \(0.70 \times 0.90 = 0.63\), so \(0.63 x = 63\) gives \(x = 100\) dollars.

questions.stem: Two investments total \(10{,}000\) dollars. One earns \(5\%\) and the other \(8\%\) simple annual interest; together they earn \(680\) dollars in one year. How much was invested at \(8\%\), in dollars?
